verses.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
verses.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

cites.point: I am placing a khalifah on earth: stewardship as purpose
The angels ask whether Allah will place on earth one who corrupts and sheds blood.
Adam made khalifah on earth: the purpose given to humanity.
Adam named a khalifah; the angels ask and are told Allah knows what they do not.
I will place a khalifah on earth.
Adam was destined for the earth before his creation.
Allah places a khalifa on earth: the first coordinate of who you are.
Allah tells the angels He will place a steward on earth: humans were made for stewardship.
Guide us to the straight path: the ethic Muslims ask for daily
'Guide us to the straight path' asked in every prayer: not a literal path but a figure of speech for incorruptibility in ethics and values.
The request for guidance at the heart of every recitation, the cure for aimlessness.
Muslims ask for a straight path rather than a destination
We ask for the straight path, a path to stay on rather than a summit
We ask to be guided along the path, not to a destination, so tazkiyah is a path walked continually.

The straight path is figurative: istiqamah as absolute moral integrity

verses.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
verses.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

cites.point: Ibrahim asks to see how Allah gives life to the dead so his heart may be at rest: evidence that he was a questioner.
Ibrahim shown the birds revived: know that Allah is Mighty and Wise
Ibrahim asks to see how the dead are revived; the birds
Ibrahim asks to be shown how Allah gives life to the dead.
Ibrahim asks to see how Allah revives the dead and is shown the birds on the mountains.
Ibrahim asks how the dead are raised; the birds
Ibrahim asks to see how the dead are revived, contrast with his silence at the sacrifice
Ibrahim asks to see how Allah gives life to the dead and is shown the birds.

verses.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
verses.en: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

cites.point: Created from a male and female into nations and tribes to know one another
The most honoured with Allah is the most pious
The noblest is the most God-conscious
Diversity exists so that people may know one another
The Prophet recites that the most honoured before Allah is the one with most taqwa, grounding the statement that no race or lineage carries merit.
The most honoured of you is the most pious
Humanity made into nations and tribes so they may know one another.

verses.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
verses.en: He it is Who hath sent among the unlettered ones a messenger of their own, to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow, and to teach them the Scripture and wisdom, though heretofore they were indeed in error manifest

cites.point: The same four objectives with purification second.

The Prophet was sent to recite the signs, purify people and teach the Book and wisdom.

verses.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
verses.en: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of the guidance, and the Criterion (of right and wrong). And whosoever of you is present, let him fast the month, and whosoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast the same) number of other days. Allah desireth for you ease; He desireth not hardship for you; and (He desireth) that ye should complete the period, and that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you, and that peradventure ye may be thankful

cites.point: Allah wants ease for you, not hardship.
Allah wants ease for you, to complete the days, glorify Him for guidance and be grateful.
Ramadan's superiority comes from being the month in which the Quran was sent down.
Ramadan's status comes from the Quran being revealed in it
Ramadan's rank comes from the Quran being sent down in it.
The only verse naming Ramadan defines it by the revelation of the Quran before mentioning fasting.

verses.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
verses.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

cites.point: The surah's central verse on obedience.
When Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, no believing man or woman has a choice in it.
The core verse of the surah: believers have no choice once Allah and His Messenger decide.
The surah's central verse on having no choice once Allah decides.
No option once Allah decides.

The foundation verse of the surah.
It is not for a believing man or woman to have a choice once Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter; whoever disobeys has clearly gone astray. The central verse of the khutbah.

verses.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشۡتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۚ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقۡتُلُونَ وَيُقۡتَلُونَۖ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡهِ حَقࣰّ ا فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَٱسۡتَبۡشِرُواْ بِبَيۡعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِي بَايَعۡتُم بِهِۦۚ وَذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
verses.en: Lo! Allah hath bought from the believers their lives and their wealth because the Garden will be theirs: they shall fight in the way of Allah and shall slay and be slain. It is a promise which is binding on Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. Who fulfilleth His covenant better than Allah? Rejoice then in your bargain that ye have made, for that is the supreme triumph

cites.point: The covenant: Allah has bought the believers' lives and wealth in return for Paradise.

'Their lives and their possessions': what the Ansar offered, and what the Quran says believers sell to Allah for Paradise.
Allah has bought the believers' lives and wealth in exchange for Paradise; dedicate yourself to Him.

Allah has bought the believers' lives and wealth for Jannah, which is impossible if something else is loved more.
Allah has bought from the believers their lives and wealth in return for Jannah, almost the wording of Aqabah.
Allah has bought the believers' lives and wealth in exchange for Jannah.

verses.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ

verses.ar: حُرِّمَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةُ وَٱلدَّمُ وَلَحۡمُ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ وَٱلۡمُنۡخَنِقَةُ وَٱلۡمَوۡقُوذَةُ وَٱلۡمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيۡتُمۡ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسۡتَقۡسِمُواْ بِٱلۡأَزۡلَٰمِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ فِسۡقٌۗ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمۡ فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِۚ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ أَكۡمَلۡتُ لَكُمۡ دِينَكُمۡ وَأَتۡمَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعۡمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمَ دِينࣰ اۚ فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ فِي مَخۡمَصَةٍ غَيۡرَ مُتَجَانِفࣲ لِّإِثۡمࣲ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
verses.en: Forbidden unto you (for food) are carrion and blood and swineflesh, and that which hath been dedicated unto any other than Allah, and the strangled, and the dead through beating, and the dead through falling from a height, and that which hath been killed by (the goring of) horns, and the devoured of wild beasts, saving that which ye make lawful (by the death-stroke), and that which hath been immolated unto idols. And (forbidden is it) that ye swear by the divining arrows. This is an abomination. This day are those who disbelieve in despair of (ever harming) your religion; so fear them not, fear Me! This day have I perfected your religion for you and completed My favour unto you, and have chosen for you as religion al-Islam. Whoso is forced by hunger, not by will, to sin: (for him) lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

cites.point: Revealed at Arafah: the completed religion signalled the end of the Prophet's life
'Today I have completed your religion for you' was heard on that day; no other faith has such a verse, so everything taught is handed forward with nothing to add.
'Today I have completed your religion for you' came down on Arafah during this Hajj; the Jew's remark to Umar and Abu Bakr's sobbing show it was understood as the peak and the farewell.
The religion is perfected, so there is no need to embellish it to impress people

Today I have perfected your religion.
The religion perfected at Arafah, signalling the end of the Prophet's mission.
This day I have perfected your religion, read as a sign the Prophet's mission was ending.

verses.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِۖ فَلۡيَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِي وَلۡيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِي لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡشُدُونَ
verses.en: And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me. So let them hear My call and let them trust in Me, in order that they may be led aright

Allah is near and answers the caller; links the name to Ramadan

verses.en: Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth

facts.claim: He was born in 1985 in the Toronto area, in Richmond Hill, Canada.
He spent early childhood in Canada, grew up in Saudi Arabia through the 1990s, and moved to his family's village in Syria in 1999.
His Syrian home was a small mountain farming village of roughly 2,800 to 3,000 people, where most residents carried his family name.
He chose to make Syria his home because his grandfather and great-grandfather were born in that village.
He describes himself as the child of a mixed marriage who never felt fully accepted anywhere: the Arab boy in Canada, the Syrian boy in Saudi Arabia, and the Canadian boy in Syria.
He says he and his whole generation in Syria were raised to keep their heads down and avoid politics, a mindset he admits he still carries.
He married in Syria at about 26 and is a father.
He learned the Quran as a young child in Saudi Arabia, continued in Syria, and had memorized it by about age 13.

At about 16 or 17 he travelled roughly an hour each way from his village to study with a sheikh in Damascus, who turned him away three weeks running before accepting him and remains his teacher today.
He earned an ijazah from a teacher he sat with for about two years, completing it at his family home around 2001 or 2002.
He entered medical school in 2004 and attended a Sharia school at the same time, with medicine in the mornings and Sharia studies in the evenings.
His medical training ran through internal medicine residency and then the specialty of medical oncology.
He says every one of his teachers earned a living from a profession such as medicine, pharmacy, engineering, accounting or business, and none took money for teaching.
In his Arabic lessons he calls the Damascus hadith scholar Nur al-Din Itr "our sheikh" and names Abdullah Siraj al-Din as a sheikh of his own sheikhs.
He credits the elderly men of his village masjid, who passed away one or two a year over about 11 years, as grandfather figures who patiently raised him and the other youth.
A soft-spoken teacher only nine or ten years his senior, who came to the village as imam around 2001, deeply shaped his understanding as a teenager.
He says his teachers trained him in freedom of thought, telling him to argue against their views and follow only what convinced him.
He counts a teacher's advice from over 20 years ago, to keep a secret good deed known only to Allah, among the most valuable things he was ever told.
He often passes on a teacher's advice to share successes with those who love you and failures only with those who truly love you.
Of the Prophet's traits, the one he holds up for himself most is relentlessness, and his lifelong habit of reading about geniuses shapes how he sees the Prophet's genius.
He says he was mentored for years by his father, his university teachers, his Quran teachers, and young men in their twenties who guided him at 15 on which scholars and university to choose.
He is a medical oncologist who works in hospitals and runs a clinic in London, Ontario.
Before leaving Syria he worked as a resident physician in a Damascus hospital until early 2013.

He began teaching Quran at 15 in a room of his house, and the program grew until 400 to 500 village children were enrolled; he describes about 15 years of youth work in Syrian masjids that his London work largely repeats.

He first led prayer as imam at about 14 and ran a village masjid by 17, but his teachers allowed him to give the Friday khutbah only in their presence at first, and he still treats it as permitted to him only where needed.
In London he first taught at the London Muslim Mosque, starting its Quran program and a weekly Sunday halaqah in 2015, and later taught at MAC Westmont from its opening year of 2019.
He opened the Muslim Wellness Network centre in London on 18 February 2022.
He founded and named the Imam Development Academy in September 2022, a parallel-learning program whose faculty includes most of the city's imams.
He organized surveys of London's Muslim community, starting with a paper survey at the London Muslim Mosque in March 2018 that gathered about a thousand responses.
He trains young men to lead taraweeh and gives new reciters a turn each Ramadan so the role passes to the next generation.
He sees his job as provoking thought rather than handing out answers, giving people a method to reach their own conclusions without steering them toward any agenda.
He puts correct understanding ahead of emotional stirring, warning that constant appeals to the heart leave people numb.
He promotes parallel learning, steady part-time study of Islam alongside school or work, which he says is exactly how he learned.
He holds that sacred knowledge must never be sold and urges imams to build separate careers so they can teach independently of boards and salaries.
He believes identity is built through mentorship and role models more than through courses, and he meets young men weekly to ask what each is contributing.
He narrates some hadith with disputed chains when his teachers accepted them, and tells his audience when he is doing so.
He teaches tazkiyah through the five pillars he was taught, including self-value, mortality and self-honesty, and insists students practise the exercises rather than only listen.
He gives a seven-episode series near the end of each Ramadan, a format he began in Syria and restarted in London in 2019, and reuses it as Imam Development Academy course material.
He has taught the full seerah many times, six times in Syria and more in London, and says he learns more from it than anyone listening.
He wants masjids to be welcoming spaces, open equitably to men and women and centred on education and mentorship, that exist only as long as they serve the community.
He urges young Muslims to enter advocacy and public institutions, seeing speaking for people who have no voice as a central purpose of Muslims living in Canada.
When his father tried to give his teacher a money gift after the ijazah, the teacher took deep offence, a moment he retells as proof that sacred knowledge has no price.
He left Syria on 21 April 2013, saying that staying had become a danger to himself and to others around him.
He arrived in London in July 2013, during Ramadan and aged 28, and says it felt as if someone pressed a reset button on his life, including a culture shock in the country of his birth.
Applying for medical residency positions in Canada over about four years, he collected thousands of rejection emails, which he still keeps in a folder.
On his first Friday as a resident he found no time set aside for Jumu'ah, so he arranged it himself, and he still steps out of work for it each week.
He knew the family killed in the June 6 attack in London very well, having seen the father at the masjid daily for years, and calls the event deeply personal.
He called the week the Syrian regime fell in December 2024 the most difficult of his life, because a reality he had built his life around was suddenly gone.

On his sheikh's instruction he served a man he had resented for years, the one who obstructed his village Quran program, and the man became a close friend who later greeted him on his return to the village.
He once advised his gentle young imam teacher to warn the hardened village farmers about Hellfire instead of speaking only of love, a lesson he retells about knowing your audience.
Two of his teachers once advised him to stick to academic writing because he did not seem suited to public speaking, and he kept trying anyway.
Every Ramadan for over 20 years he writes a personal plan with his intentions, the duas he will make in sujud, and a list for repentance.
In Ramadan he reads the Quran continuously, finishing and starting again without counting.
He prays at night every night, a habit he traces to the Prophet's praise of a companion named Abdullah that was conditioned on night prayer.
Every night he recites Quran over his children and loved ones as ruqyah.
He spends 10 to 15 minutes every day listening to an Islamic lecture series.
He journals his reflections in notebooks, and when he left Syria he filled one of his two suitcases with them.
